key_insight: The paper extends RT-TDDFT beyond the dipole approximation by keeping the full spatial structure of the electromagnetic vector potential, enabling accurate all-electron simulations of X-ray–matter interactions.
engineering_relevance: This makes it possible to model X-ray response in molecules, surfaces, and periodic solids with higher physical fidelity, including effects that standard dipole-based approaches miss.
method: Implemented full minimal coupling in FHI-aims using numeric atom-centered orbitals.
Included both paramagnetic and diamagnetic light–matter couplings with spatially resolved vector potentials.
Added reciprocal-space current diagnostics and a perturbative photon-momentum sideband scheme for periodic systems.
evidence_signal: The implementation was validated on four benchmarks spanning 100 eV to 5 keV, showing beyond-dipole effects and dipole-forbidden channels.
watch_item: The periodic-system extension relies on a perturbative photon-momentum sideband treatment, so accuracy may depend on the strength of the momentum transfer and the regime of application.
paper_title: Full Minimal Coupling All-Electron Real-Time TDDFT for X-Ray-Matter Interactions
